newsitem.title: USA: CME to start Taiwan Stock Index products on GLOBEX.
newsitem.headline: CME to start Taiwan Stock Index products on GLOBEX.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) said its board of directors has approved to list futures and options on the Dow Jones Taiwan Stock Index initially on GLOBEX electronic after-hours trading system.
A launch date for GLOBEX trading had yet to be set and a start date for pit trading would also be determined later, a CME spokeswoman said.

In October, CME offered to delay the start of the products to January 15 from its original November target in response to concerns of Taiwanese regulators that the introduction could increase volatility in Taiwan's stock market.
The CME spokewoman said, however, that that offer was not taken and a January 15 launch was never set.
"What we said is, in return for an information sharing agreement we would offer to delay a launch to January 15," she noted. "That's out of the picture."
The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission has yet to formally approve CME's Taiwan index contracts, she said.
"We are awaiting final CFTC approval," she said.
She said the CME board also agreed to a Saturday GLOBEX trading session for the Taiwan index from 1830 CST (Friday)/0230 GMT (Saturday) to 2300 CST/0500 GMT.
She said this was because the Taiwan Stock Exchange has a Saturday morning session 0900 local time (0300 GMT) to 1100 (0500 GMT).
The Taiwan Stock Exchange is planning to open its own futures exchange in July 1997.
The Dow Jones Taiwan index comprises 113 of the largest stocks traded on the Taiwan exchange. CME, Reuters Holdings Plc and Marche a Terme International de France are partners in GLOBEX.
